title: Decision Maker Checkpoint
intro: You have learned booleans, comparisons, if chains, and the and/or/not keywords. Time to prove it. Eleven rounds, one from every idea in this module. Get them right on the first try to earn ⭐⭐⭐!

rounds.prompt: Which of these is a Boolean value?
rounds.explain: A boolean is written True or False with a capital letter and no quotes. "True" in quotes is a string, and lowercase true is not defined in Python.
>= means 'greater than or equal to'. The two sides match, so the answer is True.

rounds.prompt: This is meant to compare, not store. Pick the fix.
options: Use two equals signs: if score == 10:
Remove the colon at the end
rounds.explain: One equals sign stores a value. Two equals signs compare. Inside an if you almost always want ==.

rounds.prompt: Why won't this run? Pick the fix.
rounds.explain: An if statement always needs a colon at the end of its line, before the indented block.
10 is not 13 or more, so the if condition is False and Python runs the else branch instead.

rounds.prompt: Two conditions are True here. Which one wins?
rounds.explain: Python stops at the first True condition. 12 is 5 or more, so Silver prints and the Gold check is never reached. Put the strictest condition first.

rounds.prompt: What is the result of:  True and False
rounds.explain: and is True only when both sides are True. A single False makes the whole thing False.

rounds.prompt: What is the result of:  False or True
rounds.explain: or needs only one side to be True. The right side is True, so the whole thing is True.
not has_umbrella flips False into True. So the condition is True and True, which is True, and the first branch runs.

rounds.prompt: Match each operator to what it asks.

pairs.right: Are these two exactly the same?
Is the left bigger, or equal?
Is AT LEAST ONE side True?
Flip this value to its opposite

rounds.explain: The first three compare two values and give back a boolean. The last three combine or flip booleans you already have.

rounds.prompt: Build the check: if it is raining, take an umbrella, otherwise wear sunglasses.
rounds.explain: The if line comes first with its condition, then its indented action, then else with its own indented action. Since raining already holds True or False, you can write it on its own without == True.
